title: Perf run 20261020-0008
heading: A game's first board picture comes up about a quarter sooner
meta: This speed run kept two speed changes and one fix to the benchmark, plus three tests that the review asked for. They are on branch improve/20261020-0008, from base 2f25230, with main merged in at 4b47d81. Every figure below is from software rendering (SwiftShader) on a 4-vCPU VM, and each names the commits it compares.

needs.intro: Nothing here blocks the merge. Both items are information the skill asks for, not questions.

items.title: Information: three primary rows lean slower, none called
items.body:
In the final A/B (026ac73 against 4b47d81, 8 pairs), three rows were worse in most pairs or more than 3% worse at the median pair. None is called worse.

  • Start page answers its first click, desktop: ×1.131 at the median pair, 6 of 8 pairs worse (pairs 0.93 1.06 1.57 0.89 1.07 1.44 1.19 1.53).
  • A shared game's page, first screen: ×1.061, 6 of 8 pairs worse (1.26 1.08 1.14 0.93 1.01 0.83 1.08 1.05).
  • A finished game's review, every mark in: ×1.031, 5 of 8 pairs worse (0.97 1.13 0.93 1.07 1.05 1.09 1.01 0.92).

This run changed no code on these paths except RT1's 25 bytes in the entry. The first two rows leaned the same way in earlier A/Bs of unrelated code (ledger 1009-1606:Q1 and 1016-0821:RG6), and an A/A of identical code leaned up to ±6% on about a third of the rows.
items.recommend: No decision needed. The next run's regression check reads these rows again.

items.title: Information: the 1.2× target is met on 4 of 16 rows
items.body: Joining's first board picture (×0.766), the computer's (×0.772), the player's move (×0.697) and the opponent's move (×0.795) are past 1.2× at the median pair. The other 12 rows are flat because this run's changes do not reach them: the start page, reopening, the review and the search. The biggest remaining wait, the review (2.08 s), was not attacked this run.

scoreboard.intro: The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. The dashed line is the target, 1.2× faster than the base. Each bar is a row's median pair; below 1 means faster.

items.title: Final A/B: the branch against main as merged, all 16 primary rows
items.body: 026ac73 against 4b47d81, 8 pairs, 52 minutes (ab-20261020-0008-final.md): ×1.067 over 16 rows. Two rows are called better: joining's first board picture, 1.07 s to 834 ms, and the computer's, 1.18 s to 907 ms. The player's move went 220 to 146 ms, better in all 8 pairs, but the pairs spread from 0.59 to 0.82, so the A/B does not call it on the final commit. Improve's 10-pair A/B of DR2 and DR5 called it at ×0.709, so it is reported here as a lean, not a held result. No row is called worse. Memory is flat. The start page downloads 0.8 KiB more on desktop and on the phone.

changed.intro: Each change is its own commit with its A/B report in bench/loop/.

items.title: A game's board comes up without React's reveal hold (RT1, 5ba8ed6)
items.body:
When a canvas's code had already loaded, React still suspended it once and then held the page for up to 300 ms before showing it. lazyChunk now hands React the loaded code at once, so the canvas renders in the page's first commit. The game's canvas also measures its size without r3f's 50 ms delay. The change reaches every canvas and screen loaded through lazyChunk: the game, the lobby, the tutorial and the computer game.

Against 2f25230, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-0008-rt1.md): joining's first board picture ×0.781 and the computer's ×0.766, both called better. On the final commit: ×0.766 and ×0.772, both called better. The test lazyChunk.test.tsx fails on the base's code.

charts.caption: 2f25230 against RT1's code, setup and computer sections, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-0008-rt1.md).

items.title: A frame at rest redraws a few small rects, and the shimmer only its pulses (DR2 and DR5, f825a1d)
items.body:
Before, a frame at rest redrew one rect around everything that changed. A pick's marks are spread over the tower, so that rect met most pieces, and in software rendering each piece costs its vertices. Now the frame is drawn in up to 4 smaller rects, one pass each, and each pass leaves out the pieces wholly outside its rect. The last move's shimmer now marks only the stretch its pulses light, not the whole line.

Against 4f47439, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-0008-dr2-dr5.md): the player's move 220 to 153 ms, ×0.709, called better. The opponent's move ×0.707 and a pick ×0.850 were not called. The CPU time to prepare the player's move's picture rose from 1.6 to 2.7 ms and is called worse. That is about 1 ms against about 70 ms saved. e2e damage.spec finds 0 differing pixels between these frames and the same frames drawn whole, on desktop and phone.

Trade-off: these changes add 0.8 KiB (gzip) to the scene code that the start page's preview downloads. The start page's timing rows did not move (phone usable ×0.997).

charts.caption: 4f47439 against DR2+DR5, setup, move-latency and select sections, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-0008-dr2-dr5.md).

items.title: The benchmark counts a frame's passes as one frame (4f47439)
items.body: A measurement fix that DR2 needs. Without it, the move and pick rows would time only a frame's first pass. On the base only the frame pacer renders, once per task, so the base's figures do not change.

items.title: Tests the review asked for (bef00b6, 6d4cc7f, 026ac73)
items.body: damage.test now tests passes(), with the vertices a frame draws as the count that guards DR2's gain. It fails if passes() draws one rect again, skips merging, skips its cost check, or ignores rects left from the frame before. The shimmer's glow falloff and cut-off now have one source, read by the shader, by shimmerLit and by the test. The test also checks that the shader still contains the lines it copies. Five deliberate breaks of the shader or the box each fail it. damage.spec now waits until it has compared more than 20 frames: after main's #200 made the game shorter, the phone case compared exactly 20 in one full e2e run.

removed.intro: No code was removed. Production code grew by 236 lines and lost 32 (DR2, DR5 and RT1), against 4b47d81; tests and the bench grew by 316 lines. bench/loop/patches/canvas-at-once-RT1-MEASURE.patch is deleted because RT1 is now a commit. The bench shim for bases before #172 moved from patches/ to tools/.

items.title: The waited-for frame queued behind the frame in flight (1017-0532:UF1)
items.body: 8 pairs (ab-20261020-0008-uf1.md): the player's move ×1.281, worse in 8 of 8 pairs; a pick ×1.364, worse in 7 of 8. Reverted. The likely cause is that the queued frame is the click's own frame, so in software rendering two frames of GPU work stand before the picture the player waits for.

items.title: The last move's line marks only the stretch drawn so far (0008:LB1)
items.body: 8 pairs (ab-20261020-0008-line.md): the player's move ×1.044, the opponent's ×0.976. No gain. Reverted.

items.title: A V8 compile hint on the entry (1009-0411:P3)
items.body: Cold load, 8 pairs (ab-20261020-0008-hints.md): every start-page row ×0.99 to ×1.03. No gain. Reverted.

items.title: Holding the lobby's frames while the game links its programs (JC1's premise)
items.body: Measured with temporary marks, not kept as code: about 650 ms of joining's ~830 ms first picture is SwiftShader linking the game's 26 shader programs, and holding the lobby's frames changed nothing (795 ms). This points to the next run's main bet, 0008:PR1.

items.title: Final A/B against main as merged, not the run's base
items.body: main gained six PRs during the run, including #200, which changes move timing. The final A/B compares the branch's final commit with 4b47d81 (main as merged), so it measures only this PR. Run 1841 did the same.

items.title: 8 pairs for the final A/B
items.body: 16 runs fit the stage's time. At 8 pairs the player's move was better in every pair but not called; it is reported as not called.

items.title: Review items that do not block the merge went to the ledger
items.body: New rows: 0008:PL2 (cap the pacer's pass loop), PS2 (the cost of passes() on frames with many changes), MS2 (the canvas's scroll listener), LZ1 (a chunk loaded by another importer), TR1 (triangles per move as a bench diagnostic), CR2 (the creator's first picture and one stray shader count). Notes were added to EN1, DR12, DR8, DR9, CL1, SP1 and PR1.

items.title: The breakthrough bet was not started
items.body: 0008:PR1, making the game's renderer and its 26 shader programs before the click, needs 80 to 250 lines in the lobby's handover and a 20-minute A/B. Under an hour was left, so it is the next speed run's first item.

items.title: DR2 on a real GPU
items.body: Every figure is from software rendering, where a pass costs its vertices. On a phone's GPU, several passes might cost more than one. Ledger 1019-1119:DR8 asks for a check on real phones.

items.title: DR5's own share of the gain
items.body: DR2 alone gave ×0.735 (not called) and DR2 with DR5 ×0.709 (called). They are one commit, so DR5's own effect is unknown (ledger 0008:SP1).

items.title: The ~650 ms of shader linking
items.body: The figure comes from temporary marks that are not committed. The next run redoes them before building PR1.
